title: Research method for Insomnia effector gene predictions (Watanabe et al., 2022)
bodyHtml:
These results are from the study:

Genome-wide meta-analysis of insomnia prioritizes genes associated with metabolic and psychiatric pathways.
Watanabe K, et al.
Nat Genet. 2022 Aug;54(8):1125-1132. doi: 10.1038/s41588-022-01124-w..
PMID: 35835914

The authors performed a GWAS meta-analysis of insomnia in 593,724 cases and 1,771,286 controls and discovered 554 loci with genome-wide significant associations, containing 791 independent lead SNPs. They defined credible SNPs by fine-mapping. At each locus:

  • credible SNPs were were mapped to genes if they caused deleterious coding sequence changes (nonsynonymous, stop-gain, stop-loss or splicing) or colocalized with eQTLs for the gene. eQTL results were obtained from GTEx v8, PsychENCODE, and eQTLGen.
  • for loci that did not include credible SNPs meeting those criteria, GWAS-significant SNPs were mapped to genes by the methods listed above.

Genes identified in either of these ways were termed "high-confidence" (HC) and were assigned an HC-1 classification if they were the single HC gene in a locus or an HC-m classification if they were among multiple HC genes in a locus.

Finally, protein-protein interactions between HC-1 and HC-m gene products were investigated using data from InWeb (Li et al., 2017). Genes were classified as High-confidence prioritized genes if a) they had been classified as HC-1 by the above approaches or b) were classified as HC-m AND their gene product interacted directly with an HC-1 gene product.

Chromatin interaction results, included in the sub-rows, were not considered in the prioritization method but are provided as potential additional supporting evidence.
